title: Normalized coefficient-ring localization before module transport
statement: Let l be prime, E/Q_l finite, X noetherian and finite dimensional with l invertible, and R a normalized RationalModuleRealization [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Put B equal to the completed integral coefficient sheaf, a equal to its canonical constant-section map, t equal to the fixed uniformizer, and S=B[1/a(t)] the sheafified section localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. There is an isomorphism c:S ≅ E_X of ring sheaves whose composite with B → S is R.integralIso.hom followed by R.inclusion. For every r in A[1/t] and test object U, the inverse c sends the constant rational section pbcRationalCoefficientEquiv(r) to the canonical localized scalar section scalarLocalizationCoefficientMapOfUniverses(r) on U [lem-per-rational-continuous-coefficient-derived-localization]. This statement concerns ring sheaves and their constant sections.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1)-(2), pp. 58-59; coefficient change implicit in Proposition 6.8.14(2), p. 62.

proof.text: Compare the completed constant-section map followed by R.integralIso.hom with the continuous constant-section map. R.finite_normalization identifies both maps after each finite quotient, and R.integral_normalization identifies those quotients with the reductions of continuous integral functions. The normalized inverse-limit comparison makes the reduction maps jointly monic, proving equality of these integral ring-sheaf maps and in particular equality of their uniformizer sections.

Localize the integral ring-sheaf isomorphism at the matching uniformizer sections. Inverse section maps exist by the localization universal property; uniqueness gives naturality and the inverse identities. Sheafify and compose with R.localizationIso. R.localization_normalization and R.inclusion_normalization identify the coefficient-unit composite on every integral numerator, hence as a ring-sheaf map.

The resulting isomorphism takes localized constant integral coefficients to constant field coefficients. Both scalar maps from A[1/t] agree on A. Uniqueness of localization and the canonical equivalence A[1/t] = E make them equal on every fraction. Apply the inverse ring-sheaf map to obtain the inverse formula.

from.place: Coefficient-ring comparison in the first step of ordinary rational realization localization.

lean.statement:
theorem rationalRealizationCoefficientLocalization
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    [Fact (∃ n : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim X ≤ n)]
    [Fact (∀ x : X, IsUnit (l : X.presheaf.stalk x))]
    (R : RationalModuleRealization l E X) :
    let B := pbcAdicCompletion X (pbcIntegralDatum l E)
    let a := pbcCompletedScalarSections X (pbcIntegralDatum l E)
    let t := pbcUniformizer l E
    let S := ringedLocalizationRingOfUniverses.{u + 1, u + 1, u} B (a t)
    ∃ c : S ≅ rationalCoefficientSheaf l X E,
      ringedLocalizationRingUnitOfUniverses.{u + 1, u + 1, u} B (a t) ≫ c.hom =
        R.integralIso.hom ≫ R.inclusion ∧
      ∀ (r : Localization.Away t) (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ),
        c.inv.hom.app U
          ((rationalModuleConstantMap l E X).hom.app U
            ((toSheafify (ProEt.topology X)
              ((Functor.const X.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} E)))).app U
                (ULift.up (pbcRationalCoefficientEquiv l E r)))) =
          (scalarLocalizationCoefficientMapOfUniverses (PbcIntegralRing l E)
            B a t r).val U
